title: Developers Clicked 'Don't Ask Again.' Claude Code Saved Their Passwords — and 1,122 of Those Files Are Sitting on Public GitHub.
content: Every well-run home has one rule about keys: you do not leave them in the front door. It turns out thousands of software developers have been doing exactly that, and an AI coding assistant was holding the door open for them. On November 5, the security firm Apiiro published research on Claude Code's "Yes, and don't ask again" button. That's the option a developer clicks when the assistant wants to run a shell command and they'd rather not be asked a second time. Apiiro found that when the approved command contains a password or an API key, Claude Code saves the entire command, secret included, as a permanent allow rule in a small file called .claude/settings.local.json . That file is meant to stay on your laptop. Apiiro went looking for it on public GitHub anyway, and found 104,185 copies across 103,617 repositories. What was in the files 1,122 files held real-looking secrets: 1,379 distinct credentials in the current versions alone. Counting older commits, shared settings.json files a
author: Faith & Fact - Marky Mark
summary_zh: Apiiro 的研究发现，开发者点击 Claude Code 的“Yes, and don't ask again”后，如果批准的 shell 命令里带有密码或 API Key，整条命令会连同密钥一起写进 .claude/settings.local.json，成为永久允许规则。研究人员在公开 GitHub 上找到了 104,185 份这类文件，其中 1,122 份含有明文凭据。文章提醒开发者把该文件加入 .gitignore、定期检查权限规则，并且不要在命令里直接写入密钥。

title: CLAUDE.md: How a Bloated File Inflates Your Bill
content: Why does CLAUDE.md cost so much? CLAUDE.md costs so much because it sits in the part of the prompt that gets re-sent on every single turn, and it sits at the front of the cache prefix. So a fat or unstable file gets re-billed on every request for the entire session, and a file that changes between sessions quietly invalidates prompt caching so you pay full freight instead of the ≈10% cache-read rate. No file in your repo weighs more on token cost, and almost nobody treats it that way. I spend my days building token tooling, and CLAUDE.md is the single most common own-goal I see. People obsess over whether to read a file with head or cat , then paste a 900-line house style guide into CLAUDE.md and wonder where the bill went. The big lever isn't hiding. Agent-driven commits, CI checkouts, and mirror fan-out pushed git past practical limits. content: The new status-update design for Claude Code subagents beats the old one, and it wins most clearly for people who run long, parallel background agents close to their usage limit. title: Keep Claude Code away from your .env files with permission deny rules
content: Claude Code reads files to help you. That is great, until the file is .env, a private key, or a cloud credentials folder. Permission deny rules let you block those reads outright. Minimal deny list In .claude/settings.json (shared with the team) or settings.local.json (personal), add these entries under permissions.deny: Read(./.env) Read(./.env.*) Read(./secrets/**) Read(~/.aws/**) Read(~/.ssh/**) Deny rules win over allow rules, so even if you later allow broad Read access, these paths stay blocked. title: Your Agent Remembers the Old Fact. Can It Use the Update?
content: A project changes its deployment target. A customer changes their delivery address. A teammate stops owning a service. The agent has seen the update. Weeks later, it confidently acts on the previous information. That failure is especially difficult to catch because the answer can look perfectly reasonable. title: Runtime-Enforced Agentic Systems
content: As large language models transition from text generators to autonomous agents operating across enterprise systems, the infrastructure supporting their execution becomes a critical point of failure. An agent tasked with a complex workflow might successfully reason through a multi-step process, only to fail midway due to an API timeout, a malformed tool response, or a subtle hallucination. In traditional imperative orchestration, this failure leaves the system in a corrupted, half-executed state. This creates a fundamental architectural problem: an agent's probabilistic reasoning is inherently fragile, but the enterprise systems it interacts with require absolute state consistency. The call to a database, the deployment of a service, or the dispatch of a financial transaction cannot simply be retried from the beginning without catastrophic side effects or duplicated actions. Find those routes by listing every server route, then marking the ones that call a model and the ones that check who is signed in. A route that does both, and has no check, is the one to close first. A developer read 25 public vibe-coded apps, mostly Lovable, by reading their code and git history. None had a hardcoded secret. Eleven had any server layer at all; the other fourteen were frontend-only. Two of the eleven exposed an AI-calling route with no login check and no per-user rate limit. The author calls that "n=2, not a statistic," and the sample is small. Treat it as a checklist of where to look, not as a market study. title: Claude Code Keeps Saying 'Not Logged In · Please Run /login'? I Mapped Every Login Message in 2.1.318
content: Originally published at its-tahir.com . I kept seeing two different login errors in Claude Code and assumed they meant the same thing. They don't: one means there is no credential at all, the other means Claude Code tried to renew my login and gave up. Version 2.1.318 also adds a third, for a login that hits a fixed end date. Which one have you been hitting, and how often? Claude Code shows Not logged in · Please run /login when the session has no credential it can use, and Login expired · Please run /login when it tried to renew your saved claude.ai login, the renewal was refused, and it cleared the login. Both are fixed the same way: run /login inside Claude Code, or claude auth login in a shell. Retrying without signing in shows the same message on every request. content: A/又开始作妖了，刚刚 GitHub 上爆出个让人头皮发麻的事。 ​有个哥们最近邮箱天天收到一堆乱七八糟的诈骗邮件，顺藤摸瓜抓包查本地流量，当场人傻了。 罪魁祸首是他本地终端里跑的 Claude Code 。 Claude 现在只要联网搜索资料，就会把你的真实个人邮箱直接写进 HTTP 的 User-Agent 请求头。 它每抓一个网页，你的私人邮箱就顺手送进对方的服务器日志里。 那些扫日志倒卖数据的黑产连爬虫都不用折腾，直接坐着收割。 ​更绝的是 A/官方的做法。 源码里删掉拼邮箱那行代码只要几秒钟，官方人员不这么干，跑去 Issue 里一本正经地回复，说最新版加了个隐私插件专门拦截这种行为。 自己往井里倒机油，转头大张旗鼓宣布研发出了滤水器，还当成技术特性端上来。 ​大家在本地把文件读写和系统权限放心地全交出去，结果大厂官方工具一出门就拿着你的私人信息到处乱送。 这操作连普通流氓软件看了都要直呼内行。 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/107757
author: KamenReborn
summary_zh: V2EX 帖子转述了 GitHub issue #107757，说有用户抓包后发现，Claude Code 联网抓取网页时会把用户的真实邮箱写进 HTTP User-Agent 请求头，导致邮箱进入第三方服务器日志，进而收到诈骗邮件。帖子还说官方没有直接删掉相关代码，而是在新版里加了隐私插件来拦截。这件事提醒使用 Claude Code 联网功能的开发者注意隐私泄露，但原文情绪化表述较多，技术细节需要对照原 issue 核实。

title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?
content:

2) Are you using models outside (or instead) of those subscriptions? For example, pay-as-you-go APIs, OpenRouter, or locally hosted models.

3) What coding harnesses and interfaces are you using? Are you sticking with the default CLIs or IDE integrations, or using alternatives like OpenCode, Pi, Aider, Muse Code, or custom-built harnesses?

4) Are you using any agent orchestration or swarm tools?

5) Are you using broader agent platforms like OpenClaw / Hermes Agent / Grok bot / Dots / Muse?
